sampling_model.design: Independent sampling under the induced observed law \(P_m\) for a structural mechanism \(m\in\mathfrak M_6\).
sampling_model.units: For each \(m\), the observations \(X_{1,m}^{\mathrm{obs}},\ldots,X_{n,m}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) are independent and identically distributed copies from \(P_m\).
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment; the target is the structural outer-coefficient vector \(\theta(m)=(a(m),d(m))^\top\).
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; identification strength is controlled by the observable chart, residual-Jacobian, influence-covariance, and global-separation margins uniformly over \(m\in\mathfrak M_6\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The middle coefficients and disturbance law are not estimated for identification. Empirical covariance and centered third cumulants form \(g_{n,m}\), and \(\widehat S_{n,m}\) is estimated from plug-in centered influence vectors.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper gives a necessary-and-sufficient generic direct-effect criterion for acyclic mixed graphs and only partial identification results for cyclic graphs.
The paper identifies full mixing matrices under specified higher-order tensor-zero patterns and derives pointwise optimally weighted minimum-distance inference.
The paper identifies a full structural matrix up to scaling and permutation from one diagonal higher-order source cumulant and gives pointwise root-\(n\) inference.
The paper identifies unrestricted full mixing under pairwise mean independence and proves generic nonidentification after one pairwise condition is dropped.
The paper proves that a simple directed cycle has a generic two-point covariance fiber.
The paper characterizes the maximal linear group preserving each Gaussian graphical concentration model.
The cyclic LiNG procedure returns a distribution-equivalence class under mutually independent non-Gaussian errors.
The paper establishes pointwise large-sample consistency, asymptotic normality, and optimal weighting for GMM estimators.
The paper establishes BayCausal identification under its stated disjoint-cycle framework and applies the method to the Women's Interagency HIV Study.
The paper gives a higher-order-cumulant rank criterion for causal-structure identification with latent variables in an acyclic model.

body.tldr: In the three-variable linear system with overlapping feedback pairs and a path-dependent disturbance vector, endpoint independence generates three observable residual cross-cumulants. Covariance elimination turns the two third-order restrictions into observable cubics; for a mechanism \(m\), nonvanishing of the explicit chart \(D(P_m)=v(P_m)\chi(P_m)p_3(P_m)q_3(P_m)s_1(P_m)\) makes their linear first subresultant recover the observable functional \(\theta(P_m)=\theta(m)\), with the entire complex residual fiber equal to the structural truth. A legal one-dimensional real covariance fiber makes order three minimal on a nonempty regular locus, while a two-parameter middle-residual shear leaves the complete observed law unchanged and therefore keeps \((b,c)\) as sensitivity parameters. The statistical frontier is uniform feasible optimal-weight GMM and a uniformly covering sandwich ellipse over structural mechanisms \(m\in\mathfrak M_6\), indexed coherently by their induced laws \(P_m\) and targets \(\theta(m)\).

project_justification.gap: Published dependent-error identification is complete for acyclic graphs but only partial for cycles, while existing higher-cumulant recovery assumes global source restrictions that exclude arbitrary middle-error dependence. Covariance nonidentification results do not establish the projected legal fiber required for an information-order lower bound, and nearby cumulant estimators provide pointwise rather than uniform inference.
project_justification.niche: The fixed overlapping-cycle motif permits elimination of all central coefficients and nuisance cumulants from a two-dimensional outer query. Its residual equations are small enough for an explicit subresultant chart yet rich enough to separate query identification from full-model identification.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies a rational order-three inverse \(\theta(P_m)=\theta(m)\), a legal real order-two query-moving fiber, and a complete-law central shear, then targets a uniform centered-cumulant GMM expansion and sandwich coverage over a single compact mechanism class under transparent quantitative margins.

body.related_work: Tramontano, Drton, and Etesami provide the connected-set Markov and independence-genericity framework, a complete acyclic direct-effect criterion, and only partial cyclic results; their whole-distribution transfer argument informs the residual construction but does not deliver the proposed finite-order rational map. Drton, Foygel, and Sullivant show that cyclic Gaussian covariance parametrizations can be noninjective, but their simple-cycle fiber does not establish a query-moving curve in the present non-Gaussian path-dependent class. Mesters and Zwiernik translate structured cumulant zeros into polynomial mixing restrictions and pointwise optimally weighted minimum distance; their standardized uncorrelated-source framework does not allow the middle-error cumulants retained here. Jiang identifies a full matrix from a diagonal single-order source cumulant by an eigenvector map, whereas the proposed witness has nonzero adjacent mixed third cumulants and uses sparse residual restrictions. Ribot, Seigal, and Zwiernik identify unrestricted mixing under pairwise mean independence and show failure after one pairwise restriction is dropped; that full-matrix obstruction leaves graph-constrained coordinate recovery open. Draisma, Kuhnt, and Zwiernik characterize transformation groups of Gaussian graphical models, so their theorem supplies provenance for the shear pattern but is not a cyclic non-Gaussian identification comparator. Lacerda, Spirtes, Ramsey, and Hoyer recover distribution-equivalence classes in cyclic LiNG models with mutually independent errors, a different disturbance class and target. Hansen supplies the pointwise GMM backbone, while Newey and McFadden supply compact extremum-estimator arguments; the proposed uniform centered-cumulant result adapts these tools rather than claiming to replace them. Jin and coauthors' BayCausal theorem uses disjoint cycles, so the prospective application described here is an extension outside their published guarantee, not a correction to it. Chen and coauthors give a latent-confounded higher-order-cumulant rank criterion for an acyclic model; that criterion informs the use of higher cumulants but does not subsume the fixed cyclic residual-elimination inverse or the legal real order-two fiber.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The chart \(D\neq0\) is a sufficient recovery chart, not a characterization of the full identification region. The exceptional set mixes genuine nonidentification, symmetric third-order degeneracy, degree specialization, and possible recovery by another chart. The uniform GMM expansion is the unresolved bottleneck: sixth-Wasserstein compactness of the induced-law image \(\{P_m:m\in\mathfrak M_6\}\) must be converted into a uniform centered-cumulant central limit argument, and the estimated weight, global minimizer, and sandwich matrix must be controlled simultaneously. No inference claim is made for mechanism sequences with \(D(P_m)\to0\), \(\sigma_{\min}(J_m)\to0\), or \(\lambda_{\min}(S_m)\to0\).
body.honest_scope: The proposal concerns one fixed three-variable overlapping-cycle motif and assumes that its structural zero pattern and disturbance path are independently justified. It does not learn the graph, classify every real fiber on \(D=0\), or identify \((b,c)\). The singleton residual ideal, legal covariance realization, preservation of independence genericity under the shear, and uniform GMM expansion all remain to be proved. Under centrally symmetric disturbances, third cumulants vanish, the chart correctly fails, and the model reduces to the covariance nonidentification boundary. The BayCausal and Women's Interagency HIV Study use is prospective and conditional; their published disjoint-cycle theorem is not claimed to cover this motif.
